title: Coalesce auth presets and introduce AsyncStream bridge for cross-SDK parity
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: multiple SDKs exposed similar backoff + credential preset maps and small differences in their streaming consumer surface have caused repeated bugfix PRs and user confusion. This PR centralizes a lightweight AuthPreset registry in the monorepo, exposes a compact AsyncStream bridge (AsyncStreamFacade) with minimal lifecycle hooks, and aligns the Python/TypeScript/Go SDK layering so downstream teams get the same ergonomic primitives and preset names.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces internal/auth/presets: registry + loader with JSON-first presets and environment override support.
- Adds an AsyncStreamFacade abstraction in runtime/streams/async_stream_facade.go and equivalent adapters in sdks/* to provide a single observable lifecycle for streaming consumers (start/heartbeat/finish/error) and a small ReconnectHint callback.
- Maps existing SDK-specific backoff profiles into the new preset names (fast, balanced, durable) and wires them into the SDK retry builders.
- Small ergonomic API surface changes in SDKs: Python gets a with-stream context manager; TS gets a single .stream() async iterator wrapper; Go gets a StreamHandle interface that mirrors the other two. These are additive wrappers over current APIs to minimize churn.
- Bumps SDK versions in the package metadata: python -> 1.9.0, typescript -> 2.3.1, go -> 1.7.2.

Rationale and constraints:
- Avoided heavy structural refactors: new facade is a thin adapter layer and is feature-flagged behind SDK opt-in until 2.3.1/1.9.0/1.7.2 are published.
- Presets are stored as JSON under internal/auth/presets/*.json to make it easy for infra teams to suggest tweaks without code changes.

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests added for registry loader, preset fallback behavior, and AsyncStream lifecycle hooks across sdks/python and sdks/typescript mock adapters.
- Integration smoke test added that exercises a full streaming session with simulated token expiry and verifies reauth + replay semantics.
- Cross-SDK parity job run locally to validate same behavior when using the central presets.

Checklist: 
- [x] Spec and design doc linked in Linear (ENG-9876)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] SDK examples updated (python/ts/go examples/simple_stream.py / examples/stream_iterator.ts / examples/stream_handle.go)
- [x] Release notes entry
- [x] Version bumps locked in package manifests

Backward compatibility: All changes are additive. Existing code paths continue to work. The new presets require opt-in until the next minor SDK release; we will flip the default after one release cycle once telemetry shows no regressions.

Rollout plan: publish SDKs in coordinated release; enable opt-in flag in hosted runtime for a canary group; monitor stream error rates and reauth metrics for 48 hours before wider rollout.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2026-02-15 after approvals from Diego, Priya, Owen
release_notes: Add a central Auth Preset registry and an Additive AsyncStreamFacade to unify stream ergonomics and retry presets across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs. Opt-in behind SDK flags until next minor releases (py 1.9.0, ts 2.3.1, go 1.7.2).
notes_for_backport: No backport required - additive and feature-flagged. Backport to release branches only if customer requests opt-in before next minor.
example_snippet:
# Python example: using the async facade
from redwood import StreamFacade
with StreamFacade.from_config('balanced') as s:
    for chunk in s.stream('...'):
        print(chunk)
